decks.title: Elections and the Election Commission — Part 1: Elections, and the Election Commission
goals: Explain what an election is and why it is essential in a representative democracy
Distinguish direct from indirect election with Indian examples
Describe the composition, appointment and term of the Election Commission
Explain how the independence of the Election Commission is protected

slides.heading: Elections and the Election Commission
slides.body_md: Part 1 — how **voters choose**, and who makes sure the choice is **fair**.

visual.alt: Route map of Part 1: the meaning of elections, direct and indirect elections, the Election Commission and how its independence is protected
visual.caption: Part 1 at a glance

slides.narration: In a democracy the people choose those who govern them. They do this through elections. But somebody must make sure that elections are fair. In this part we learn what an election is, how direct and indirect elections differ, and how the Election Commission is formed and protected.

slides.heading: What is an election?
bullets: A process in which **voters choose** representatives by voting.
Held at regular intervals, for a fixed term of office.
Voters can **choose again** or **change** their representatives.

visual.alt: Flow: voters cast votes, representatives are chosen, and a government is formed that remains answerable to the voters
visual.caption: What an election does.

slides.narration: An election is the method by which voters choose their representatives. It is held at regular intervals, and each representative serves for a fixed term. When the term ends, the voters get a fresh chance to keep their representatives or to choose different ones.

slides.heading: Why elections are essential
slides.body_md: In a representative democracy the people rule **through** their representatives.

rows: They choose representatives to decide for them
They must face the voters again after a fixed term
A government that fails can be voted out
One adult, one vote, whatever caste, wealth or gender

visual.alt: Table of four needs and how elections meet them: choosing representatives, keeping leaders answerable, peaceful change of government, and an equal voice for every adult

slides.narration: In a large country the people cannot all sit together and decide every matter. So they choose representatives. Elections make leaders answerable, because they must face the voters again. They allow a government to change peacefully. And they give every adult an equal voice, with one vote each.

slides.heading: Direct and indirect elections
slides.body_md: In a **direct** election voters choose the member; in an **indirect** one, **electors** do.

visual.caption: Direct and indirect elections.

slides.narration: In a direct election, the voters themselves choose the member. The Lok Sabha, the Legislative Assemblies and the panchayats are chosen this way. In an indirect election, voters or members first choose electors, and the electors choose the office holder. The President, the Vice President and the Rajya Sabha members from a State are chosen this way.

slides.heading: Quick check: why elections matter
slides.body_md: Which feature is missing where rulers are never chosen by the people?
slides.narration: Think about what elections give to the people in a representative democracy. Then choose the option that names what is missing in the imagined country of Ardanya.

slides.heading: Who is elected how

visual.alt: Table of five offices or bodies, the method of election of each, and who chooses: Lok Sabha, Legislative Assembly and panchayat directly by voters; Rajya Sabha State seats by MLAs; President and Vice-President by electors

slides.narration: Here is a table to remember. Lok Sabha members and members of the Legislative Assemblies are directly elected by the voters of each constituency. Panchayat members are directly elected by ward voters. Rajya Sabha members from a State are elected by the elected members of the Assembly of that State. The President and the Vice President are chosen by electors.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: direct or indirect?
slides.body_md: Ask who makes the final choice: the voters or electors.
bullets: Step 1 — Find who casts the vote that decides the winner.
Step 2 — If it is the voters themselves, the election is **direct**.
Step 3 — If elected members or electors decide, it is **indirect**.
Step 4 — Write the reason in one line.

rows: Ward voters of Kesarwadi mark ballots for a panchayat member
Ward councillors of Ambarpet choose a board chairperson
Lohitgarh MLAs vote to send a member to the Rajya Sabha
MLAs, not voters at large, choose

visual.alt: Table sorting three imagined cases: ward voters choosing a panchayat member is direct, councillors choosing a chairperson is indirect, and MLAs sending a member to the Rajya Sabha is indirect

slides.narration: Use a simple test. Ask who casts the vote that decides the winner. If the voters themselves do, the election is direct. If elected members or electors decide, it is indirect. Ward voters choosing a panchayat member is direct. Councillors choosing a chairperson is indirect. Assembly members choosing a Rajya Sabha member is also indirect.

slides.heading: The Election Commission of India
slides.body_md: Elections need a fair **umpire**.

rows: To superintend, direct and control elections

visual.alt: Table of facts about the Election Commission: set up under Article 324 on 25 January 1950, observed as National Voters' Day, an independent constitutional body whose job is to superintend, direct and control elections

slides.narration: The Election Commission is an independent body created by the Constitution. It was set up under Article three twenty four, on the twenty fifth of January nineteen fifty. This date is now observed as National Voters Day. Its job is to superintend, direct and control elections.

slides.heading: Composition of the Commission
bullets: A **Chief Election Commissioner** (CEC) and such other **Election Commissioners** as the President fixes.
Since **1993**: the CEC and **two** Election Commissioners.
Appointed by the **President**; term **six years or age 65**, whichever is earlier.

Since nineteen ninety three it has had three members, the Chief and two Commissioners. They are appointed by the President. The Chief serves for six years, or until sixty five years of age, whichever comes first.

slides.heading: Appointment: the dated note
slides.body_md: Appointment rules can change; always note the **year**.

rows: The CEC and such other Election Commissioners as the President fixes; three since 1993
Six years or until age 65, whichever is earlier

A 2023 Act provides a selection committee: the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or leader of the largest opposition party)

slides.narration: The President appoints the members. As of twenty twenty four, a law of twenty twenty three provides that the President acts on the recommendation of a selection committee. The committee has the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister chosen by the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha. Remember to write the year when you give this point.

From nineteen ninety three, it has had three members. In twenty twenty three, a law set up a selection committee for appointments. This was the position as of twenty twenty four.

slides.heading: Quick check: removing a Commissioner
slides.body_md: How may an Election Commissioner other than the CEC be removed?
slides.narration: Think about who can recommend such a removal. It is not the government alone.

slides.heading: Keeping the Commission independent
bullets: The **CEC** can be removed only like a **Judge of the Supreme Court**.
Service conditions cannot be made **worse** after appointment.
Other Commissioners are removed only on the **CEC's recommendation**.

nodes.label: CEC removable only like a Supreme Court Judge
Service conditions not made worse after appointment
Other Commissioners removed only on the CEC's recommendation

visual.alt: Flow of three safeguards for independence: the CEC can be removed only like a Supreme Court Judge, service conditions cannot be made worse after appointment, and other Commissioners can be removed only on the CEC's recommendation
visual.caption: Three safeguards of independence.

slides.narration: The ruling party also contests elections, so the Commission must not be under its control. The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the way a Supreme Court Judge is removed. Service conditions cannot be changed to the disadvantage of the Chief after appointment. Other Commissioners can be removed only if the Chief recommends it.

bullets: **Election:** voters choose representatives; **direct** (Lok Sabha, Assemblies, panchayats) or **indirect** (President, Vice-President, Rajya Sabha).
**Commission:** Article **324**, **25 January 1950**; CEC and two Commissioners since **1993**.
Appointed by the **President**; term **six years or age 65**.
**Independence:** difficult removal, protected service conditions.

bullets: Define an election in one line, then give its **need**.
For direct and indirect, give **one example** of each and say who the **voters or electors** are.
Write **Article 324** and **25 January 1950** together.
Add "as of 2024" when you mention the 2023 selection committee.
Do not quote Articles; give their meaning in your own words.
slides.narration: Some exam habits. Define an election in one line, then give its need. For direct and indirect elections, give an example of each and say who the voters or electors are. Link the Article and the date together. When you mention the selection committee, say that it is the position as of twenty twenty four. Paraphrase the Articles.

slides.heading: What the Commission does, and kinds of elections
slides.body_md: Part 2 — the **work** of the Commission, the **Code of Conduct**, and **three kinds** of elections.

visual.alt: Route map of Part 2: the functions of the Election Commission, the Model Code of Conduct, general and mid-term elections, and by-elections
visual.caption: Part 2 at a glance

slides.narration: In this part we see what the Election Commission actually does, from preparing the voter lists to conducting the poll. We study the Model Code of Conduct. And we learn the difference between a general election, a mid-term election and a by-election.

slides.heading: Functions of the Commission

rows: Prepare and revise electoral rolls; issue EPIC photo identity cards
Recognise parties; allot symbols; supervise nominations and their scrutiny
Fix the schedule; conduct polling with voting machines and paper trail; appoint observers

sections.heading: 1. What an election is, and why it matters
sections.body_md:
- An **election** is the process by which **voters choose** representatives or office-holders by casting votes.
- In a **representative democracy** the people rule through representatives, since they cannot decide every matter themselves.
- Elections are held at **regular intervals** for a **fixed term**; leaders must face the voters again.
- They let a government be **changed peacefully** and give every adult citizen an **equal voice** (one adult, one vote).

key_terms.definition_md: The process by which voters choose representatives or office-holders.
A democracy in which the people rule through elected representatives.

rows: They choose representatives to decide for them

A government that fails can be voted out
One adult, one vote, whatever caste, wealth or gender

sections.heading: 2. Direct and indirect elections
sections.body_md:
- **Direct election:** the voters themselves choose the member. Examples: **Lok Sabha**, **Legislative Assembly**, **panchayat** members.
- **Indirect election:** voters or members choose **electors**, and the electors choose the office-holder. Examples: the **President** and the **Vice-President** (electoral college); **Rajya Sabha** members from a State (elected by that State's **elected MLAs**).
- Test: ask **who casts the deciding vote**, the voters or electors.
- Panchayat and municipal polls are held by **State Election Commissions**.

sections.heading: 3. The Election Commission: set-up, composition, appointment
sections.body_md:
- Set up under **Article 324** on **25 January 1950**; the date is now **National Voters' Day**.
- Its job is to **superintend, direct and control** elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President.
- **Composition:** the **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)** and such other **Election Commissioners** as the President fixes. Briefly multi-member in **1989-90**; **three members** (CEC and two) **since 1993**.
- **Appointed by the President.** **As of 2024**, a **2023 Act** has a selection committee: the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha (or leader of the largest opposition party).
- **Term:** six years or until age **65**, whichever is earlier.

sections.heading: 4. How independence is protected
sections.body_md:
- The ruling party also contests elections, so the Commission must be an **independent umpire**.
- The **CEC** can be removed only in the manner of a **Supreme Court Judge**.
- **Conditions of service** of the CEC cannot be changed to the CEC's **disadvantage** after appointment.
- **Other Commissioners** can be removed only on the **recommendation of the CEC**.
- Independence still needs honest conduct, a free press and informed citizens.

key_terms.definition_md: Freedom from control or pressure by the government of the day.

sections.heading: 5. Functions of the Commission and the Model Code
sections.body_md:
- **Voters:** prepares and revises the **electoral rolls**; issues **EPIC** photo identity cards.
- **Parties and candidates:** **recognises** parties, allots **symbols**, supervises **nominations** and their scrutiny.
- **Polls:** fixes the **schedule**, conducts polling (voting machines with a paper trail slip), appoints **observers**, sees to counting and results.
- **Not its job:** redrawing constituency boundaries (a separate **Delimitation Commission**) and panchayat polls (State Election Commissions).
- **Model Code of Conduct:** guidelines for parties and candidates from the **announcement of the schedule** to the **results**; its purpose is **free and fair** elections and no **misuse of official machinery**.

sections.heading: 6. General election, mid-term election and by-election
sections.body_md:
- **General election:** all seats of a House are filled after its **full term** (five years for the Lok Sabha and a State Legislative Assembly).
- **Mid-term election:** all seats are filled **before the term ends**, after the House is **dissolved early**.
- **By-election:** **one seat** is filled after it **falls vacant** through **death, resignation or disqualification**; generally held **within six months**.
- To name an election, **count the seats** and ask **why**.

questions.stem_md: Which statement best describes an election in a democracy?

options.text_md: A process in which the oldest member of a community becomes the ruler
A process in which voters choose their representatives or office-holders by casting votes
A process in which a ruler names a successor from the family
A process in which officials are picked by a draw of lots among all citizens

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** A process in which voters choose their representatives or office-holders by casting votes. An election is the method by which voters choose representatives or office-holders through voting. Rule by the eldest, by family succession or by a draw of lots does not involve the voters making a choice among candidates.

questions.stem_md: In the imagined country of Ardanya the people never vote; their rulers are chosen by one family. Which feature of a representative democracy is missing there?

options.text_md: A flag and an anthem
A capital city with a large assembly hall
Taxes collected from citizens
Elections that let the people choose and change those who make decisions for them

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** Elections that let the people choose and change those who make decisions for them. In a representative democracy the people rule through chosen representatives, and elections are how they choose them and remove them. A flag, an assembly hall or taxes may exist under any kind of government, so they do not mark out a democracy.

questions.stem_md: Which one of the following bodies has its members elected directly by the voters?

options.text_md: The Lok Sabha
The Rajya Sabha (members from the States)
The office of the President
The office of the Vice-President

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** The Lok Sabha. Lok Sabha members are elected directly by voters in their constituencies. Rajya Sabha members from the States are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies, and the President and the Vice-President are elected by electors, so those three are indirect.

questions.stem_md: At a polling booth in the imagined village of Kesarwadi, every adult resident marks a ballot paper for one of five candidates for the village panchayat seat of her ward. What kind of election is this?

options.text_md: An indirect election
A nomination without a vote
A direct election
An election of electors only

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** A direct election. The voters choose the candidate themselves, with no intermediate electors, so it is a direct election. It is not indirect because no group of electors stands between voters and the winner, and it is not a nomination because a vote takes place.

questions.stem_md: In the imagined district of Ambarpet, voters elect forty ward councillors, and these councillors then vote among themselves to choose the chairperson of the district board. How should the choice of the chairperson be described?

options.text_md: Direct election, because voters first elected the councillors
Neither, because chairpersons are never elected
Indirect election, because the voters' choice passes through elected councillors
A general election, because forty seats are involved

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Indirect election, because the voters' choice passes through elected councillors. The chairperson is chosen by elected councillors and not by the voters themselves, so this stage is indirect. The councillors alone were chosen directly. A general election is the renewal of a whole House, not the choice of one office-holder.

questions.stem_md: A student prepares a table of four imagined entries. Which entry matches a body with the wrong method of election?

options.text_md: Legislative Assembly: indirect election by the Lok Sabha
Lok Sabha: direct election by voters of each constituency
Rajya Sabha (State seats): indirect election by MLAs
Panchayat member: direct election by the voters of a ward

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** Legislative Assembly: indirect election by the Lok Sabha. Members of a Legislative Assembly are elected directly by the voters of their constituencies, not by the Lok Sabha, so that row is wrong. The other three rows state correct methods.

questions.stem_md: True or false? When the voters of the imagined ward of Mirzakhel mark a ballot for their own panchayat member, that is an example of direct election.

options.text_md: True
False

questions.solution_md: **True.** Voters choose the member themselves with no electors in between, so the election is direct.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Regular elections help citizens of the imagined State of Samudrapur to change a government that has failed them.

**Reason (R):** In a representative democracy those who govern are chosen by the voters for a fixed term.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: (A) is true and (R) is false.
(A) is false and (R) is true.
Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Both are true. Because representatives hold office only for a fixed term and are chosen by voters, the voters get a regular chance to replace a government, which explains the assertion.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The Rajya Sabha members of a State are elected by indirect election.

**Reason (R):** They are chosen directly by all adult voters of the State.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: (A) is true and (R) is false.
(A) is false and (R) is true.
Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (a)** A is true: they are elected by the elected MLAs of the State. R is false because adult voters at large do not choose them.

President

questions.stem_md: What is meant by an election? Why is it needed in a representative democracy?
questions.solution_md: Meaning, then the need.

answer.model_answer_md: An **election** is the process in which **voters choose** their representatives by voting. It is needed because in a representative democracy the people **cannot rule directly**, so they elect people to govern on their behalf.

questions.stem_md: Distinguish between direct and indirect election.
questions.solution_md: Contrast with one example each.

answer.model_answer_md: In a **direct election** the **voters themselves** choose the representative, as for the Lok Sabha. In an **indirect election** the voters or members first choose **electors**, who then choose the office-holder, as for the President.

questions.stem_md: In the imagined Lohitgarh, (a) citizens vote to choose a member for the State Legislative Assembly and (b) the elected assembly members then vote to send a representative to the Rajya Sabha. Name the type of election in each case.
questions.solution_md: Classify each case with its reason.

answer.model_answer_md:

questions.stem_md: Sort the following into direct and indirect elections and give a reason: (a) members of the Legislative Assembly, (b) the Vice-President, (c) a ward member of a panchayat.

questions.stem_md:
Elections are the lifeline of a representative democracy.

(i) What is an election, and why is it essential in a representative democracy? **[3]**
(ii) Distinguish direct election from indirect election. **[3]**
(iii) Give two examples of each kind of election in India and explain who the voters or electors are in each example. **[4]**
questions.solution_md: Meaning and need; contrast; examples with voters or electors.

answer.model_answer_md:
(i) An **election** is the process by which voters choose representatives by voting. In a **representative democracy** the people cannot make every decision themselves, so they elect representatives, hold them **answerable**, and can **change** them at the next election.

(ii) In a **direct election** the **voters themselves** choose the representative. In an **indirect election** the voters or members choose **electors** first, and the electors choose the office-holder.

(iii) **Direct:** Lok Sabha members, chosen by the voters of each constituency; panchayat members, chosen by the voters of a ward. **Indirect:** the President, chosen by an **electoral college** of elected members; Rajya Sabha members from a State, chosen by that State's **elected MLAs**.

questions.stem_md: Under which Article of the Constitution of India is the Election Commission set up?

options.text_md: Article 352
Article 368
Article 21
Article 324

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** Article 324. The Election Commission derives from Article 324, which places the superintendence, direction and control of elections in it. Article 352 deals with emergencies, Article 368 with amendment of the Constitution and Article 21 with protection of life and personal liberty.

questions.stem_md: How is the Election Commission of India made up?

options.text_md: A single judge of the Supreme Court
A Chief Election Commissioner and such other Election Commissioners as the President may fix
The Prime Minister and the Cabinet
All the Chief Ministers of the States

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (b)** A Chief Election Commissioner and such other Election Commissioners as the President may fix. The Commission has a Chief Election Commissioner and such other Election Commissioners as the President may fix from time to time. questions.stem_md: Rao is appointed Chief Election Commissioner in an imagined year when she is exactly 63 years and 6 months old. For how long can she hold the office?

questions.stem_md: In what manner can the Chief Election Commissioner be removed from office?

questions.stem_md: How may an Election Commissioner other than the Chief Election Commissioner be removed?

By the Chief Minister of any State
Only on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner
By the Election Commissioners themselves, by a vote

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (c)** Only on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner. questions.stem_md: The government of the imagined country of Veluvanam proposes to cut the salary and allowances of its serving Chief Election Commissioner because the Commission refused to postpone a poll. Which safeguard of independence is being tested?

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** The rule that service conditions cannot be changed to the CEC's disadvantage after appointment. The CEC is not required to be a retired judge, is appointed not elected, and Commissioners do not serve for life.

questions.stem_md: A student lists four arrangements about the Election Commission. Which one does NOT help to keep the Commission independent?

Conditions of service cannot be made worse after appointment
The Prime Minister may dismiss the CEC whenever a poll result is disliked

questions.solution_md: **Correct option: (d)** The Prime Minister may dismiss the CEC whenever a poll result is disliked. The 2023 Act provides a selection committee of three: the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition (or the leader of the largest opposition party) in the Lok Sabha. The other bodies named have no such role. This describes the position as of 2024.

questions.stem_md:
The Election Commission is the guardian of free and fair elections.

(iii) Explain how the independence of the Commission is protected. **[4]**
questions.solution_md: Article and date; composition, appointment and term; safeguards.

answer.model_answer_md:
(i) It is set up under **Article 324** of the Constitution, on **25 January 1950**, a date now observed as **National Voters' Day**.

(ii) It has a **Chief Election Commissioner** and such other **Election Commissioners** as the President fixes; since **1993** there are two. They are appointed by the **President**; as of 2024 this follows the recommendation of a **selection committee** under a law of 2023. The CEC serves **six years or until age 65**, whichever is earlier.

(iii) The **CEC** can be removed only like a **Supreme Court Judge**. Conditions of service cannot be changed to the CEC's **disadvantage** after appointment. Other Commissioners can be removed only on the **CEC's recommendation**. These rules keep the Commission free from fear of the government.

questions.stem_md:

answer.model_answer_md:

(ii) Other Commissioners can be removed only on the **CEC's recommendation**, so the government cannot dismiss them directly.

(iii) The safeguards make it hard to **punish** the Commission for firm decisions, so they help neutrality. But the way members are **chosen** matters as well, so a transparent selection and honest **conduct** by the members are needed, together with **public scrutiny**, a free press and courts that can examine disputes.

questions.stem_md: During which period does the Model Code of Conduct apply?

Only on the day of polling
Throughout the five years between elections

questions.stem_md: Two days after the Commission announces the schedule for the imagined State of Lohitgarh, a minister inaugurates a new bridge using a government vehicle and announces a new grant for voters of his constituency. What does the Model Code of Conduct expect?

options.text_md: Nothing, because ministers are exempt from the Code
That the minister should be allowed to announce more grants on polling day
That official machinery and new announcements by the government should not be used to favour any party
That the Code applies only to candidates who are not ministers

questions.stem_md: A student lists the work of the Election Commission as: preparing electoral rolls, allotting symbols, appointing observers and choosing the winning candidate in each constituency. Which item is wrongly included?

answer.model_answer_md:

answer.model_answer_md: A **by-election** is held when a single seat **falls vacant** through the death, resignation or disqualification of a member. It is generally held **within six months**.

questions.stem_md: In the imagined State of Ambarpura, (a) a member of the Assembly resigns to take up another office, and (b) the Assembly is dissolved two years early. Name the election each will lead to.
questions.solution_md: Classify each with a reason.

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) A **by-election** in the constituency of the member who resigned.
(b) A **mid-term election**, because the whole Assembly must be elected again before the usual term ends.

questions.stem_md: Distinguish a general election, a mid-term election and a by-election.
questions.solution_md: One point per type.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. A **general election** fills **all seats** of a House after its **full term**.
2. A **mid-term election** fills **all seats** after the House is **dissolved early**.
3. A **by-election** fills **one seat** that has fallen **vacant**.

(b) **Yes**, because **disqualification** vacates the seat.
(c) **Yes**, because **resignation** vacates the seat.
In each case it is generally held **within six months**.

questions.stem_md: Some people say a mid-term election is a waste of money; others say it is a democratic remedy. Give one point for each view and one point on what it shows about elections.
questions.solution_md: One point each way and one lesson.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. **Waste:** a fresh poll for all seats costs the **public money** and effort.
2. **Remedy:** when no stable government can be formed, the voters get the chance to **decide again**.
3. It shows that in a democracy, **authority returns to the people** in a crisis.

questions.stem_md:
Elections to a legislature are held in different situations.

(i) What is a general election? When is it held? **[3]**
(ii) Explain a mid-term election and the circumstances in which it is held. **[3]**
(iii) Explain a by-election, with the causes and the usual time within which it is held. **[4]**
questions.solution_md: General; mid-term; by-election with causes and time.

answer.model_answer_md:
(i) A **general election** is one in which **all the seats** of a House are filled. It is held when the House **completes its full term**, which is five years for the Lok Sabha and for a State Legislative Assembly.

(ii) A **mid-term election** is held **before the end of the term**, after the House has been **dissolved early**, for example when no party can form a stable government. All seats are contested again and the new House gets a fresh term.

(iii) A **by-election** fills a **single seat** that has fallen **vacant** through the **death**, **resignation** or **disqualification** of the member. Only the voters of that constituency vote. It is generally held **within six months** of the vacancy.

questions.stem_md:
In the imagined constituency of Taralpur, the member of the State Assembly dies, and the Commission announces a poll. Rahul, who turned eighteen last month, wants to vote.

(i) Name the kind of election that will be held and state when it is generally held. **[3]**
(ii) What must Rahul do to be able to vote, and which body prepares the electoral roll? **[3]**
(iii) The schedule has been announced. Explain two ways in which the Model Code of Conduct and the Commission will make the poll fair. **[4]**
questions.solution_md: Kind of election and time; roll and EPIC; Code and Commission.

answer.model_answer_md:
(i) A **by-election**, since a single seat is vacant by **death**. It is generally held **within six months** of the vacancy.

(ii) Rahul must see that his **name is on the electoral roll**, and apply to be added if it is not; the roll is prepared and revised by the **Election Commission**, which also issues the **EPIC** card.

(iii) The **Model Code of Conduct** applies from the announcement until the result; the governing party cannot misuse **official machinery** or make **fresh announcements** to win votes. The Commission appoints **observers**, supervises nominations and conducts the poll, so voters in Taralpur choose without pressure.

marking_scheme.step: (ii) Name on the roll, apply if missing
